issue.title: Avoid Needless Forking when Closing Transports

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
No need to fork off in the changed spots if we block the calling thread anyway. All this does is make tests less deterministic and (in case of the fire and forget forking to `GENERIC`) introducing potential resource leaks if things are released in transport handlers.

Also, some other minor cleanups of dead code.

body: I think we hit exactly this problem in https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/3lq4o3iswxumo/console-log?task=:server:test which seems like an odd coincidence since this isn't a new bug and yet I've not seen it result in test failures ever before.

issue.title: Notify stubbable transport behaviors on clear

labels.name: >test
labels.description: Issues or PRs that are addressing/adding tests

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
If `MockTransportService#addUnresponsiveRule` adds a rule that drops
requests to a node then we must notify the rule on removal so that the
requests don't leak. Today we notify rules when removing them from a
specific address but not if clearing all rules. This commit addresses
that.

Closes #77751

issue.title: Reject openConnection attempt while closing

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Today while the `ClusterConnectionManager` is closing it will reject
attempts to open _managed_ connections (i.e. using `connectToNode`), but
it still permits ad-hoc connections (i.e. using `openConnection`). This
commit extends the existing refcounting mechanism to cover both cases,
preventing all concurrent connection attempts while shutting down.

Closes #86249
Relates #77539

body: Note that #86315 means we no longer need to protect against connection attempts while closing. Should we just remove this (buggy) protection mechanism instead of trying to fix it?
